title: Applied ML Eval & Onboarding Integrated Playbook
author: Ava Chen
content:
Summary
This playbook consolidates Redwood's recommended end-to-end process for model onboarding, evaluation harness usage, prompt set and benchmark management, quantization profile validation, quality guardrails, and regression triage. It is intended for ML engineers, applied ML researchers, and platform engineers responsible for getting models into production in Redwood Dedicated/Private and for validating hosted model catalog entries.

Scope
- Applies to all model families and variants that will be served by Redwood (open weights and internally curated variants).
- Covers onboarding from initial candidate evaluation to production rollout and regression monitoring.
- Includes integration points with the eval-harness service, CI gating, and runtime telemetry.

Owners and Roles
- Playbook owner: Applied ML Platform (eng team)
- Model owner: team that proposes the model (ML or product team)
- Eval harness steward: Applied ML Infra
- Release owner: Serving Runtime Product

Key Service Names and Artifacts
- eval-harness (internal service): used to run standardized automated eval suites and regression checks.
- prompt-registry: canonical storage for prompt sets and benchmark definitions (tagged by workload and domain).
- quant-profiles (S3/Artifact store): collection of validated quantization settings per model/variant.
- onboarding-ci (GitHub Actions): CI pipeline that gates model artifacts before upload to model-catalog.
- model-catalog: internal registry with versioned model artifacts, metadata, and performance profiles.

High-level Process (end-to-end)
1. Candidate evaluation (local + eval-harness):
   - Use the eval-harness to run the standardized benchmark suite listed in the prompt-registry.
   - Minimum gate: latency and token-efficiency profile, basic safety checks, and accuracy on task-specific holdouts.
   - CLI example: eval-harness run --model-path /tmp/model --benchmarks prompt-registry://nlp/intent-detection --out results.json
2. Prompt-set curation and labeling:
   - Curate prompt sets per workload following the prompt-sets guideline. Include positive/negative examples, edge cases, and adversarial prompts.
   - Tag prompt sets with: workload, domain, languages, and risk_level.
3. Quantization validation: 
   - Select candidate quantization profile from quant-profiles (e.g., 4-bit PTQ, 8-bit QAT).
   - Run quantization-A/B evals: full functional tests, accuracy delta <= 2% absolute (or task-specific threshold), latency improvement >= 1.2x vs FP16.
   - Example table of quant profile validation criteria:

   | Profile | Expected Accuracy Delta | Expected Latency Change | Use Case |
   |---------|------------------------:|------------------------:|----------:|
   | 8-bit PTQ | <= 1% | ~1.05x | Low-risk throughput optimizations |
   | 4-bit PTQ | <= 2% | ~1.6x | High-throughput where slight quality loss acceptable |
   | 4-bit QAT | <= 0.8% | ~1.4x | Production-critical workloads (requires retraining) |

4. Quality guardrails and safety checks:
   - Run the safety and hallucination suite defined in prompt-registry://safety/core.
   - Must pass the safety suite with no critical regressions; medium-severity issues require triage before rollout.
   - Define per-model runtime guardrails config (examples below).

Runtime guardrails example (config table):

   | Guardrail | Threshold / Rule | Action | Owner |
   |-----------|------------------|--------|-------|
   | Toxicity score | < 0.7 for public-facing routes | Block + escalate | Applied ML |
   | Hallucination heuristic | > 0.3 on factual tasks | Route to fallback model or external verifier | Serving Runtime |
   | Latency P95 | < 250 ms | Auto-scale or degrade to cheaper variant | SRE |

5. CI gating and model-catalog entry:
   - Required artifacts: model weights, model metadata (architecture, tokenizer, vocab), quant profiles tested, eval results (JSON), prompt-set IDs used, training data provenance statement, license.
   - Onboarding CI checks (examples): checksum validation, eval-harness pass, license check, container scan.
6. Staged rollout and monitoring:
   - Canary: 1-5% traffic for 24-72 hours with close monitoring of latency, error rate, and quality metrics derived from eval prompts and production sampling.
   - Metrics to track: task accuracy, top-k correctness, safety incidents, perplexity drift, latency P50/P95, cost-per-token.
   - Automatic rollback triggers: >2% absolute drop in task accuracy vs baseline, >50% increase in safety incidents, latency P95 > SLO for >15 minutes.

Regression Triage Playbook (when a regression is detected)
1. Triage window (first 60 minutes):
   - Alerting system annotates the incident with model version, recent deployments, traffic-routes, and active quant profile.
   - On-call engineers run the quick checklist: reproduce locally via eval-harness with the same prompt set, check telemetry for model-serving errors, review recent changes to tokenization, post-processing, or prompt templates.
2. Isolate scope:
   - Determine whether regression is model-internal (weights/quantization) or external (prompt change, input distribution shift, runtime bug).
3. Mitigation steps (ranked):
   - Immediate rollback to last-known-good model-variant.
   - Switch traffic to a fallback model (lower-capacity but validated).
   - Apply prompt sanitization rules if input distribution changed.
4. Root cause and fix:
   - If model change: run a diff of eval-harness outputs between versions, inspect attention/logit patterns if applicable, and re-run quantization experiments.
   - If runtime bug: open a P0 ticket with serving runtime and include reproducer.
5. Post-incident:
   - Run a full regression analysis (see Regression Triage template) and update prompt-registry with any new adversarial cases.

Evaluations and Benchmarks (practical guidance)
- Benchmarks must be tagged with intent (functional, safety, latency, cost).
- Each model onboarding must include at minimum: one functional benchmark per target workload, one safety suite run, and latency/cost profiles under expected load.
- Use stratified sampling from the prompt-registry to ensure coverage across languages, modalities, and corner cases.

Eval-harness integration best practices
- Use reproducible seeds and environment containers identical to CI.
- Store eval results as JSON with metadata fields: model_version, bench_id, datetime, seed, hardware_profile.
- Standard eval command (example): eval-harness run --bench prompt-registry://<bench-id> --model model-catalog://<model-id>:<version> --save results/<model-id>_<bench-id>.json

Automated alerting thresholds (suggested defaults)
- Functional accuracy drop: 1.5% absolute -> notify, 2.5% absolute -> auto-rollout halt and page on-call.
- Safety incidents: 5 incidents / 10k requests -> notify, 20 incidents / 10k -> page.
- Latency: P95 > SLO for 10 minutes -> notify, for 30 minutes -> auto-scale or switch traffic to fallback model.

Documentation and artifacts to attach to model-catalog entry
- 1-page onboarding summary (owner, use-cases, known limitations)
- Eval results (all bench JSONs)
- Quantization profiles tested and recommended default
- Prompt-set IDs and canonical prompt examples
- Rollout playbook references and rollback points

Maintenance and periodic re-evaluation
- Scheduled re-runs: every 30 days for high-traffic models, 90 days otherwise.
- Triggered re-runs: major infra changes, tokenizer/version changes, or new security alerts.

Appendix A: CI gating checklist (short)
1. Model artifact checksum validated
2. Eval-harness full-suite pass
3. Safety suite pass (no critical failures)
4. Quant profile documented and tested
5. Licensing and data provenance verified
6. Container image vulnerability scan <= high severity 0

Appendix B: Triage contact matrix
- Applied ML (owner) -> Pager: applied-ml-oncall@redwood.example.com
- Serving runtime -> Pager: serving-runtime-oncall@redwood.example.com
- SRE -> Pager: sre-oncall@redwood.example.com

Related references
- See: prompt-sets-and-benchmarks-guidelines-2026 for prompt curation templates.
- See: quantization-profiles-best-practices-2026 for detailed quant config examples.
- See: eval-harness-onboarding-and-regression-playbook-2026 for CI integration examples.

This playbook should be reviewed quarterly and updated to reflect new model families, hardware profiles, and evolving safety guidance.
